claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets are primarily governed by variations in local lattice distortion.
Differences in atomic size misfit produce the relevant variations in local lattice distortion.
Changes in dislocation dissociation, stacking-fault energy, and CRSS are plausible mediators of mechanical behavior in FCC CrMnFeCoNi.
Removing Mn or another constituent alters local bonding and lattice parameters.
Composition-induced changes in bonding and lattice parameters change dislocation-core structure and slip-system activation.
Changes in dislocation-core structure and slip activation cause variations in strength-ductility trade-offs and failure behavior.
Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi can have a single-phase FCC structure.
Analogous quaternary and ternary subsets can all be prepared as single-phase FCC alloys under similar thermomechanical processing.
Selected constituent-removal or content-variation alloys will be prepared and compared after nominally identical processing.
Testing will be conducted at room temperature under quasi-static loading using methods including nanoindentation, micropillar compression, tensile testing, TEM, and diffraction.
Atomic-size-misfit variation induces changes in local lattice distortion and stacking-fault separation.
CrMnFeCoNi contains dissociated Shockley partial dislocations with stacking-fault separations of approximately 3.5-8 nm and a stacking-fault energy of 30 ± 5 mJ/m².
Room-temperature bulk CRSS in CrMnFeCoNi is approximately 33-43 MPa.
Increasing local distortion raises solid-solution strengthening and CRSS and alters stacking-fault energy.
Reducing constituent count generally reduces local lattice distortion and the barriers to dislocation motion.
Relative to equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi, lower-constituent-count subsets with lower distortion will have lower CRSS and hardness and may have improved ductility.
Subsets that maintain or increase atomic-size mismatch may have greater strength but less uniform plastic deformation.

The proposed relationship is limited to comparably processed, single-phase FCC alloys tested at room temperature under quasi-static deformation and may differ at extreme temperatures, in multiphase material, or under dynamic loading.
A failure of CRSS, strength, and ductility to correlate directionally with measured lattice distortion and stacking-fault energy would falsify the proposed governing relationship.
